author: Bjorn Deade
title: A Virginia woman gets Wendy's chicken nuggets for lunch. Then claims she discovers a fly baked inside one: ​'I'm literally sick' - NewsBreak
text:
By Bjorn Deade ,
5 hours ago "Wendy's" by JeepersMedia is licensed under CC BY 2.0. A Virginia woman recently shared a bizarre experience involving a Wendy’s order after she said she found what appeared to be a fly inside one of the chicken nuggets she received. As reported by BroBible , the customer, who goes by Brina (@brinnaaab), shared the experience in a TikTok video that has amassed more than 1.6 million views, 91,000 reactions, and 5,300 comments.
In the video, a receipt showed that she ordered a four-piece chicken nugget meal through Uber Eats from a Wendy’s in Chesapeake, Virginia. After receiving the order, she bit into one of the nuggets before recording her food and showing what appeared to be an insect baked into it. She later concluded that it was a fly, leaving her shocked by what she had found. She wrote in the caption, “I’m literally sick.”
The video has since drawn mixed reactions from viewers, with some questioning whether the insect was actually baked into the nugget. One commenter wrote, “I hate to say I don’t believe you but you mean to tell me the fly survived being frozen? and then deep fried?” Meanwhile, others expressed concern over the discovery, saying, “I would’ve threw up soo much I’ll be the weight I was at birth ”
Wendy’s employee responds to the alleged fly discovery Amid the mixed reactions to Brina’s video, BroBible reached out to a Wendy’s employee who said they worked at the Chesapeake location where she received her order. The employee described the alleged discovery as “extremely disgusting and disturbing” and said the franchise planned to increase its food-safety precautions. These measures could include inspecting products before preparation and ensuring bags stored in the freezer are properly sealed.
@brinnaaab No I’m literally sick wtffff I inhaled like 2 before I bit into that one 🫪
♬ original sound – Brina Flies can pose a contamination risk in restaurants because they may carry microorganisms from garbage and other contaminated areas onto food or surfaces where food is prepared. Fox Pest Control recommends keeping preparation areas clean, removing waste regularly and addressing areas where flies can enter or breed to help prevent contamination.
This is not the first recent complaint involving Wendy’s food. In August, according to The New York Post , a Chicago woman sued the fast-food chain, alleging that she became ill after eating a cheeseburger that she claimed was contaminated with bacteria. The lawsuit claimed the incident left her hospitalized twice, with her medical expenses reportedly reaching $93,578.24.
Other customers have also reported unusual discoveries in their fast-food orders. A McDonald’s customer previously claimed she found a worm moving inside her drink , while a separate Panda Express customer said she discovered a live spider inside the wrapper of a fortune cookie . In Hong Kong, another diner allegedly found a newborn rat in the satay sauce served with her takeout meal.
